key_insight: The paper shows that local thermal properties of strongly interacting SYK and related mean-field spin-glass models can be estimated in polynomial time classically at all constant temperatures up to the glass transition.
engineering_relevance: This narrows the practical gap between quantum and classical simulation for important many-body systems, and suggests new polynomial-time tools for thermal inference and Hamiltonian learning.
method: Develops a fully rigorous quantum cavity method.
Uses it to prove polynomial-time classical estimation of local Gibbs-state observables at constant temperatures.
Extends the approach to a quantum algorithm for learning SYK Hamiltonians from Gibbs-state samples.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical complexity result: local observables can be estimated in polynomial time for all constant temperatures, and the learning algorithm has polynomial time and sample complexity.
watch_item: The result is provably efficient for constant temperatures and local observables, so it may not directly extend to nonlocal quantities, finite-size numerics, or temperatures outside the stated regime.
paper_title: Polynomial-time classical algorithms for mean-field models up to the glass transition
